review_status: draft v1 - deep offshore reef jack profile

profile.behavior: Deepwater pelagic jack that schools around deep wrecks, offshore oil platforms, and steep shelf ledges.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, favorable for almaco jack.
factors.value_notes: No traceable wild-population thermal-preference study was located that validates the configured 20–28 °C range or 22–26 °C ideal. UF/IFAS reports 26 °C as a captive broodstock conditioning temperature, which is not evidence of wild habitat preference. Retain the current band only as an unvalidated screening assumption.

factors.reason_template: Structure is {value}, where almaco jacks school.
factors.value_notes: NOAA describes association with rocky outcrops and reef structures and notes artificial reefs as important habitat for transient predators. UF/IFAS documents use of artificial reefs, wrecks, and high-relief structures. These sources support the broad structure association but do not validate the exact category ranking or map scores.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in deep reef and wreck zone.
factors.value_notes: NOAA reports a 15–110 m depth range; UF/IFAS reports 3–35 m in subtropical regions and use of artificial reefs/wrecks to 245 m; the STRI account reports 3–340 m. These sources support broad depth use but do not validate the configured 30–200 m band or 40–120 m ideal for the relevant South Florida population. Depth is an active gate.

text.day: It is full daylight, when fish feed actively.

text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
